validated_results.title: Anti-Inflammatory Diet Index and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study evaluating the association between an anti-inflammatory diet index and incident renal cell carcinoma.

extraction.population: Swedish Mammography Cohort and Cohort of Swedish Men

sample_size.excerpt: Among 71,421 participants, 431 RCC cases were identified during a 19.7-year follow-up.

cases.excerpt: Among 71,421 participants, 431 RCC cases were identified during a 19.7-year follow-up.

effect_size.excerpt: Higher AIDI scores were associated with a lower RCC risk (HR for Q4 vs. Q1: 0.68, CI: 0.52–0.89).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The associations were slightly attenuated but remained significant when using baseline AIDI (1997), with HRs between 0.59 (95% CI: 0.45–0.77) and 0.68 (95% CI: 0.52–0.89).

p_value.excerpt: The most substantial reduction was seen in the highest AIDI quartile (HR: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.11, 0.63), with a p-value for trend at 0.02.

comparison.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quintile of AIDI (Q1, score 0–5), those in the highest quintile (Q4, score 8–14) had a 31–43% lower risk of RCC
comparison.location: Results / AIDI and RCC incidence, paragraph 1

design.excerpt: In this study we aimed to examine the impact of dietary inflammatory potential on RCC risk in a Swedish population-based cohort study

timing.excerpt: Follow-up started January 1 st 1998 and ended at the time of any cancer (except for melanoma skin cancer), date of death, date of emigration, or the end of follow in December 2020

continent.excerpt: The SMC was established in 1987 and consisted of all women born between 1914 and 1948 who lived in Västmanlands and Uppsala counties in Sweden’s central healthcare region

ethnicity.excerpt: Data from two Swedish cohorts, the Swedish-Mammography-Cohort and the Cohort-of-Swedish-Men, were analysed.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: For diet assessment, a 96-item food frequency questionnaire (FFQ), designed to reflect Swedish dietary habits and assess food consumption over the past year, was used at baseline in 1997 and then in 2009.
exposure_measurement.location: Methodology / The Anti-Inflammatory Diet Index (AIDI), paragraph 1

gender.excerpt: In total, the final study population included in the main analyses comprised 71,421 participants, out of whom 35,267 were women and 36,154 were men.

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale

cases.excerpt: This group comprised 283 men (105 with localised RCC and 84 with advanced RCC) and 148 women (43 with localised RCC and 62 with advanced RCC). In 137 cases (94 men and 43 women) the stage of the disease could not be established, owing to missing information from before 2004.

effect_size.excerpt: In sex-stratified analyses (p-for heterogeneity = 0.006), the association was stronger in among women (HR: 0.47, CI: 0.30–0.75) but less clear in among men (HR: 0.83, CI: 0.63–1.24).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The analysis revealed a statistically significant trend showing that higher adherence to an anti-inflammatory diet was associated with a reduced risk of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) among women, with the most substantial protective effect observed in the highest AIDI quartile (HR: 0.47, 95% CI: 0.30, 0.75) in the fully adjusted model (Table 2b ).
